clue.text: Way of working AC/DC stories we hear into rally

indicators.note: what we hear is speech, so the word for stories is taken by its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: MO is modus operandi, Latin for a way of working
AC/DC is slang for bisexual, shortened to BI
stories are lies, and the ending -LISE is said the same way

explanation.surface: A rock fan's description of how AC/DC's legends draw the crowds to a big rally.
explanation.walkthrough: AC/DC looks like the rock band (fitting the band theme) but is old slang for bisexual.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally troops or supporters is to gather and organise them for action, which is what mobilising means.

clue.text: Vincent Simmons's strand of DNA

blocks.note: first meaning: the first name shared by rock singers ... Vincent and ... Simmons of Kiss
second meaning: a hereditary unit carried on a chromosome

explanation.walkthrough: The possessive reads as if one person called Vincent Simmons owns some DNA; in fact it is the shared forename of two different musicians, and also a 1990s Britpop band.
explanation.definitionFit: A gene is a stretch of a chromosome's DNA coding for one inherited trait, loosely a strand of it.

clue.text: Fashion line presenters ultimately?

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the final letter of the preceding word is kept

blocks.note: to fashion something is to model or shape it
the last letter of presenters

explanation.surface: A question about who, in the end, shows off a designer's new range.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: models are the people who present a fashion line on the catwalk.
explanation.definitionFit: Catwalk models are the people who show a designer's collection to the audience, so they present each fashion line.

clue.text: Flight that can't have happened

blocks.note: first meaning: an escape, as from a crime scene
second meaning: the exclamation of disbelief '...!'

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a description of a cancelled plane journey; the second half is the incredulous cry spoken as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A getaway is an escape or flight, and 'Get away!' is an informal cry meaning you do not believe what you heard.

clue.text: Second player on baseball field done for

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second
the pitcher is the baseball fielder who throws to the batter

explanation.surface: A baseball line-up where the number two player out on the field is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: SPITCHER is old naval slang, found in Chambers, for something ruined or finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Spitcher is a rare slang adjective meaning ruined or finished, the same as being done for.

clue.text: Bars want lean baloney sandwiches

indicators.note: something that sandwiches holds a filling between its two outer layers

blocks.note: first half of BS, slang for baloney or nonsense
to want is to lack
a ship that leans to one side lists
second half of BS, wrapped round the rest

explanation.surface: Pubs that ask for thin bologna sausage in their sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: BS is slang for bull, nonsense, which is what baloney means; 'want' here is the old sense of lacking, not desiring.
explanation.definitionFit: To blacklist people is to bar or ban them, and as a verb bars matches blacklists in person and tense.

clue.text: Black knight captures to counter

indicators.note: a piece that captures another takes it inside, so these letters hold the next word

blocks.note: jet is a glossy black stone, so jet-black
taken as written
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A chess move in which a dark knight takes a piece in reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black knight' is a single unit here: the colour and the chess piece together hold the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: A jetton is a token or counter used in gaming or casting accounts.

clue.text: Shaft British champion from behind with shout of approval

indicators.note: reading from behind means starting at the back, so the word runs the other way

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for British
a champion is a hero
the bullring's cry of olé

explanation.surface: A British sports star cheered on from the back of the crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A borehole is a narrow shaft drilled into the ground, for water or oil.

clue.text: Crushed Yank chopped ecstasy in Palladium

indicators.note: something chopped has had its end cut off, so the last letter goes
in places one thing inside another, here inside the metal's symbol

blocks.note: to yank is to pull hard
first letter of PD, the chemical symbol for palladium
E is slang for the drug ecstasy
second letter of PD, closing round E

explanation.surface: An American cutting up drugs at the London Palladium gets crushed.
explanation.walkthrough: Palladium looks like the London theatre but is the element, symbol PD.
explanation.definitionFit: To pulp something is to crush it to a soft mass, so pulped means crushed.

clue.text: Send message to jam makers about excellent setter

blocks.note: the WI is the Women's Institute, a British women's organisation famous for making jam
RE means about or concerning; the message is regarding the excellent setter, Tack himself

explanation.surface: The setter cheekily urges you to write to the jam makers praising him.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'about' supplies letters; 'excellent setter' is the subject of the message, Tack's joke at his own expense.
explanation.definitionFit: To wire someone is to send them a telegram, an old form of urgent message.

clue.text: Make stretchy laces tie at dances

indicators.note: letters that dance move about and change places with each other

blocks.note: the fodder, ten letters

explanation.surface: Instructions for tying shoes that will stretch on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: To elasticate a garment is to fit it with elastic so that it can stretch.

clue.text: Brownies bring food items about eleven

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so these letters go round the number

blocks.note: pies are items of food
XI is eleven in Roman numerals, also a cricket or football team

explanation.surface: Girl Guides turning up with snacks at about eleven o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: Brownies look like junior Guides or chocolate cakes, but here they are the household sprites of folklore.
explanation.definitionFit: Brownies are helpful household elves of Scottish folklore, close kin to pixies as small mischievous sprites.

clue.text: Collapsed Lung dine on hollow chocolate treat

indicators.note: a hollow thing has nothing in the middle, so only the outside letters stay
something collapsed has fallen into a jumble, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written for the fodder
the first and last letters of chocolate

explanation.surface: A patient with a collapsed lung tucking into a chocolate Easter egg.
explanation.definitionFit: An indulgence is something enjoyed as a luxury, a treat one allows oneself.

clue.text: Band that is excluded previously has gone platinum

indicators.note: excluded means left out, so the abbreviation for that is drops from the band's name
gone in the sense of gone wrong or off, so the letters are muddled
previously means earlier, so this piece is placed in front of the other

blocks.note: fodder for the scramble
Blondie, the New York new-wave band
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A band that was dropped earlier has gone on to sell a platinum record.
explanation.walkthrough: Platinum in the music-industry sense is a sales award; here it is the hair colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Platinum blond and ash blond are both very pale, silvery shades of fair hair.

clue.text: Did new opener to gig, with New Order's Ceremony?

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept
a new order is a fresh arrangement, so the letters are put in a different sequence

blocks.note: taken as written for the fodder
the first letter of gig

explanation.surface: A support act asking whether it played the New Order song Ceremony at the start of the gig.
explanation.walkthrough: New Order looks like the Manchester band, whose song Ceremony completes the picture; the question mark marks the definition as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding is one example of a ceremony, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Wiping out born batsman once focus goes

indicators.note: the focus is the central point, and when it goes the middle letter is removed

blocks.note: né is French for born, used of a man's original name
Mike Gatting, former England cricket captain and batsman

explanation.surface: A former batsman, born to it, loses concentration and is wiped out.
explanation.walkthrough: GATTING has seven letters, so its focus is the fourth, a T.
explanation.definitionFit: Negating something cancels it out or nullifies it, the same as wiping it out.

clue.text: Serpent's fantastic here!

indicators.note: fantastic suggests something fanciful and transformed, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, with the 's read as is

explanation.surface: An excited cry announcing that an amazing snake has arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', linking the anagram to its definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To be present is to be here, in attendance, as when answering a roll call.

clue.text: Brought up terribly, turn out rude

indicators.note: something done terribly is done badly, so the letters come out jumbled
out in the sense of wrong or disordered tells us the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: first part of the fodder
second part of the fodder

explanation.surface: A complaint that badly raised children grow up rude.
explanation.definitionFit: A child who has been nurtured has been raised and cared for, that is, brought up.

clue.text: Specials end up supporting Arctic Monkeys primarily? Flipping nonsense!

indicators.note: a supporting act plays before the headliners, so this piece goes in front
primarily means first of all, so only the first letters of the band's two words are kept
flipping something over turns it the other way round, so the whole run of letters is read backwards

blocks.note: S stands for special, doubled for the plural as PP is pages
taken as written
the first letters of Arctic and Monkeys

explanation.surface: Imagine the ska band The Specials ending up as the support act for Arctic Monkeys: what rubbish!
explanation.walkthrough: The Specials and Madness were both 2 Tone ska bands. A support band plays before the headliners, so its letters come first, and then the whole string flips.
explanation.definitionFit: Madness can mean foolish or senseless behaviour, so it stands for nonsense as in 'that's madness'.

clue.text: Justification of lay people on guitar periodically

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every other letter is taken

blocks.note: the even-placed letters of these words

explanation.surface: A defence of amateurs strumming guitars every so often.
explanation.definitionFit: An apologia is a formal written defence of one's beliefs or conduct, a justification.

clue.text: Gangster pursues demure chief

indicators.note: one who pursues follows behind, so the gangster's name comes after

blocks.note: prim means demure and proper
Al Capone, the archetypal gangster

explanation.surface: A mobster chasing a modest gang boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Primal means first or most important, so it can stand for chief as an adjective.

clue.text: Amplifiers lifted acoustic sound Eddie Rabbitt supplied principally

indicators.note: principally means first and foremost, so only the opening letters count

blocks.clueFragment: lifted acoustic sound Eddie Rabbitt supplied
blocks.note: the first letters of these six words

explanation.surface: Country singer Eddie Rabbitt's acoustic sound was stolen for amplifiers.
explanation.walkthrough: Laser is an acronym of light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation, so lasers are, literally, amplifiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser amplifies light by stimulated emission, which is what the acronym's letters spell out.

clue.text: Some Zulus travel for five year periods

indicators.note: some means only part of, so the answer is a piece of the following words

blocks.note: inside zuLUS TRAvel

explanation.surface: Zulu travellers who go away for five years at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: A lustrum was the five-yearly Roman purification after a census, hence any five-year period; lustra is the plural.

clue.text: Swingers perhaps broadcast Ben Stiller's lover initially swapping with Tack

indicators.note: swapping means exchanging one thing for another, so a letter is replaced
broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are strewn into a new order
'initially' keeps only the first letter of 'lover'

blocks.note: the actor's name, with 's read as has
the first letter of lover
Tack is the setter, who refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: Gossip that Ben Stiller's partner swapped with the setter, like swingers.
explanation.walkthrough: One L in STILLER is replaced by I, and the ten letters are then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Libertines are people of loose morals, and swingers who swap partners are one example.

clue.text: Obscure celeb luring crowds

indicators.note: the outer words crowd round the answer, holding it tightly inside them

blocks.note: inside celeB LURing

explanation.surface: A little-known celebrity attracting large crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: Obscure looks like an adjective describing the celeb; it is a verb, and crowds is the hiding verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To blur something is to make it indistinct, which is to obscure it.

clue.text: Witness eclipse

blocks.note: first meaning: to be present at, and so witness, an event
second meaning: to outdo or surpass

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as an instruction to watch the sun go dark; the first sense splits the answer into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To beat a rival is to outshine or surpass them, and to be at an event is to see it happen.

clue.text: One hunts criminal by river in Cornwall

indicators.note: by means next to, so one piece sits alongside the other

blocks.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall, the English county at the south-west tip
a con is a convict, a criminal

explanation.surface: A manhunt for a crook hiding by a Cornish river.
explanation.definitionFit: A falcon is a bird of prey, so a predator that hunts other creatures.

clue.text: "Go away to grasp English!" editor shrieked

indicators.note: to grasp something is to hold it within, so these letters close around another

blocks.note: scram is a curt order to go away
E is the abbreviation for English
ED is the abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor screams at a writer to clear off and learn some English.
explanation.definitionFit: To scream is to shriek, so screamed and shrieked are past-tense synonyms.
